sanskrit: dvaipāyanaprabhṛtayas tathaiveme tapodhanāḥ ṛṣayaḥ suvratā dāntāḥ śṛṇvantu gadatas tava
english: Let these sages too, rich in austerity—Dvaipāyana foremost among them—men of noble vows and self-restraint, listen as you speak.

sanskrit: dhruvāya nandine hotre goptre viśvasṛje 'gnaye mahābhāgyaṃ vibho brūhi muṇḍine 'tha kapardine
english: Tell us, O mighty one, of the high glory of him who is the Unmoving, the Giver of joy, the Sacrificer, the Protector, the Creator of all, who is Fire itself—of the Shaven-headed and the Matted-locked one.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca na gatiḥ karmaṇāṃ śakyā vettum īśasya tattvataḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: The course of the Lord's deeds cannot be known in its truth.

sanskrit: hiraṇyagarbhapramukhā devāḥ sendrā maharṣayaḥ na vidur yasya nidhanam ādiṃ vā sūkṣmadarśinaḥ sa kathaṃ naramātreṇa śakyo jñātuṃ satāṃ gatiḥ
english: The gods, led by Hiraṇyagarbha and Indra, and the great sages of subtle vision, do not know his end nor his beginning. How then could he, the goal of the good, be known by a mere man?

sanskrit: tasyāham asuraghnasya kāṃś cid bhagavato guṇān bhavatāṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi vrateśāya yathātatham
english: Yet of that blessed Lord, the slayer of the asuras, the master of all vows, I shall recount to you some of his attributes, as faithfully as I am able.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktvā tu bhagavān guṇāṃs tasya mahātmanaḥ upaspṛśya śucir bhūtvā kathayām āsa dhīmataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, the blessed Lord Kṛṣṇa sipped water, made himself pure, and began to relate the attributes of that great-souled and wise one.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca śuśrūṣadhvaṃ brāhmaṇendrās tvaṃ ca tāta yudhiṣṭhira tvaṃ cāpageya nāmāni niśāmaya jagatpateḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: Listen, O foremost of brāhmaṇas, and you too, dear Yudhiṣṭhira; and you, son of the River, attend to the names of the Lord of the world.

sanskrit: yad avāptaṃ ca me pūrvaṃ sāmbahetoḥ suduṣkaram yathā ca bhagavān dṛṣṭo mayā pūrvaṃ samādhinā
english: How in time past I gained, for the sake of Sāmba, that which is most hard to win, and how the blessed Lord was once beheld by me through deep meditation—

sanskrit: śambare nihate pūrvaṃ raukmiṇeyena dhīmatā atīte dvādaśe varṣe jāmbavaty abravīd dhi mām
english: After Śambara had been slain of old by the wise son of Rukmiṇī, when the twelfth year had passed, Jāmbavatī said to me—

sanskrit: pradyumnacārudeṣṇādīn rukmiṇyā vīkṣya putrakān putrārthinī mām upetya vākyam āha yudhiṣṭhira
english: Beholding the little sons of Rukmiṇī—Pradyumna, Cārudeṣṇa and the rest—and herself longing for a son, she came to me and spoke, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: śūraṃ balavatāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ kāntarūpam akalmaṣam ātmatulyaṃ mama sutaṃ prayacchācyuta māciram
english: "Grant me without delay, O Acyuta, a son who is valiant, foremost among the strong, lovely in form, free of all blemish, the equal of yourself."

sanskrit: na hi te 'prāpyam astīha triṣu lokeṣu kiṃ cana lokān sṛjes tvam aparān icchan yadukulodvaha
english: "For there is nothing in the three worlds beyond your reach; should you wish it, you could create other worlds, O upholder of the Yadu line."

sanskrit: tvayā dvādaśa varṣāṇi vāyubhūtena śuṣyatā ārādhya paśubhartāraṃ rukmiṇyā janitāḥ sutāḥ
english: "Living on air and wasting away for twelve years, by propitiating the Lord of creatures, you begot upon Rukmiṇī her sons."

sanskrit: cārudeṣṇaḥ sucāruś ca cāruveṣo yaśodharaḥ cāruśravāś cāruyaśāḥ pradyumnaḥ śaṃbhur eva ca
english: "Cārudeṣṇa and Sucāru, Cāruveṣa and Yaśodhara, Cāruśravas and Cāruyaśas, Pradyumna, and Śaṃbhu as well—"

sanskrit: yathā te janitāḥ putrā rukmiṇyāś cāruvikramāḥ tathā mamāpi tanayaṃ prayaccha balaśālinam
english: "Even as those sons of fair prowess were begotten of Rukmiṇī, so grant to me also a son endowed with strength."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ codito devyā tām avocaṃ sumadhyamām anujānīhi māṃ rājñi kariṣye vacanaṃ tava sā ca mām abravīd gaccha vijayāya śivāya ca
english: Urged in this way by the lady, I said to the fair-waisted one: "Give me leave, O queen; I shall do as you ask." And she said to me: "Go, for victory and for blessing."

sanskrit: brahmā śivaḥ kāśyapaś ca nadyo devā manonugāḥ kṣetrauṣadhyo yajñavāhāc chandāṃsy ṛṣigaṇā dharā
english: "May Brahmā, Śiva, and Kāśyapa, the rivers, the gods who follow the mind, the fields and the herbs, the bearers of the sacrifice, the sacred metres, the hosts of sages, and the Earth—"

sanskrit: samudrā dakṣiṇā stobhā ṛkṣāṇi pitaro grahāḥ devapatnyo devakanyā devamātara eva ca
english: "the oceans, the sacrificial fees, the chants, the constellations, the ancestors, the planets, the wives of the gods, the daughters of the gods, and the mothers of the gods—"

sanskrit: manvantarāṇi gāvaś ca candramāḥ savitā hariḥ sāvitrī brahmavidyā ca ṛtavo vatsarāḥ kṣapāḥ
english: "the cosmic ages of the Manus, the cattle, the Moon, Savitṛ, Hari, Sāvitrī and the knowledge of Brahman, the seasons, the years, the nights—"

sanskrit: kṣaṇā lavā muhūrtāś ca nimeṣā yugaparyayāḥ rakṣantu sarvatra gataṃ tvāṃ yādava sukhāvaham ariṣṭaṃ gaccha panthānam apramatto bhavānagha
english: "the moments, the instants, the hours, the wink-spans of time, and the turning of the ages—may they guard you wherever you go, O Yādava, bringer of joy. Go your way unharmed and watchful, O sinless one."

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛtasvastyayanas tayāhaṃ; tām abhyanujñāya kapīndraputrīm pituḥ samīpe narasattamasya; mātuś ca rājñaś ca tathāhukasya
english: Thus blessed by her with rites of well-being, having taken leave of that daughter of the lord of the apes, I went to her father, that best of men, to her mother, and to King Āhuka—

sanskrit: tam artham āvedya yad abravīn māṃ; vidyādharendrasya sutā bhṛśārtā tān abhyanujñāya tadātiduḥkhād; gadaṃ tathaivātibalaṃ ca rāmam
english: and laid before them what the deeply grieving daughter of the lord of the Vidyādharas had asked of me; then, sore at heart, I took leave of them, and of Gada and of mighty Rāma as well.

sanskrit: prāpyānujñāṃ gurujanād ahaṃ tārkṣyam acintayam so 'vahad dhimavantaṃ māṃ prāpya cainaṃ vyasarjayam
english: Having obtained the leave of my elders, I called to mind Tārkṣya; he bore me to Himavat, and upon reaching it I dismissed him.

sanskrit: tatrāham adbhutān bhāvān apaśyaṃ girisattame kṣetraṃ ca tapasāṃ śreṣṭhaṃ paśyāmy āśramam uttamam
english: There upon that noblest of mountains I beheld wondrous sights, and I saw a holy ground supreme among the seats of austerity, a most excellent hermitage—

sanskrit: divyaṃ vaiyāghrapadyasya upamanyor mahātmanaḥ pūjitaṃ devagandharvair brāhmyā lakṣmyā samanvitam
english: the divine hermitage of the great-souled Upamanyu, son of Vyāghrapad, honoured by gods and gandharvas, endowed with a sacred and Brahmic splendour.

sanskrit: dhavakakubhakadambanārikelaiḥ; kurabakaketakajambupāṭalābhiḥ vaṭavaruṇakavatsanābhabilvaiḥ; saralakapitthapriyālasālatālaiḥ
english: It was rich with dhava, kakubha, kadamba and coconut trees; with kurabaka, ketaka, jambu and pāṭala; with banyan, varuṇaka, vatsanābha and bilva; with sarala, kapittha, priyāla, sāla and palm;

sanskrit: badarīkundapunnāgair aśokāmrātimuktakaiḥ bhallātakair madhūkaiś ca campakaiḥ panasais tathā
english: with jujube, kunda and punnāga, with aśoka, mango and atimukta, with bhallātaka, madhūka, campaka and breadfruit;

sanskrit: vanyair bahuvidhair vṛkṣaiḥ phalapuṣpapradair yutam puṣpagulmalatākīrṇaṃ kadalīṣaṇḍaśobhitam
english: graced with woodland trees of many kinds bearing fruit and flower, strewn with blossoming shrubs and creepers, made lovely with thickets of plantain.

sanskrit: nānāśakunisaṃbhojyaiḥ phalair vṛkṣair alaṃkṛtam yathāsthānavinikṣiptair bhūṣitaṃ vanarājibhiḥ
english: It was adorned with trees whose fruits gave food to birds of many sorts, and beautified with rows of woodland set each in its fitting place.

sanskrit: ruruvāraṇaśārdūlasiṃhadvīpisamākulam kuraṅgabarhiṇākīrṇaṃ mārjārabhujagāvṛtam pūgaiś ca mṛgajātīnāṃ mahiṣarkṣaniṣevitam
english: It teemed with deer, elephants, tigers, lions and panthers; was thronged with antelope and peacocks, beset with wildcats and serpents, frequented by herds of beasts of many breeds, by buffaloes and bears.

sanskrit: nānāpuṣparajomiśro gajadānādhivāsitaḥ divyastrīgītabahulo māruto 'tra sukho vavau
english: There a pleasant breeze blew, laden with the pollen of many flowers, perfumed with the ichor of elephants, and filled with the songs of celestial women.

sanskrit: dhārāninādair vihagapraṇādaiḥ; śubhais tathā bṛṃhitaiḥ kuñjarāṇām gītais tathā kiṃnarāṇām udāraiḥ; śubhaiḥ svanaiḥ sāmagānāṃ ca vīra
english: With the murmur of cascades and the cries of birds, with the auspicious trumpeting of elephants, with the lofty songs of the kiṃnaras, and the holy sounds of those who chant the Sāman, O hero—

sanskrit: acintyaṃ manasāpy anyaiḥ sarobhiḥ samalaṃkṛtam viśālaiś cāgniśaraṇair bhūṣitaṃ kuśasaṃvṛtam
english: —it was such as others could not so much as conceive in the mind; adorned with lakes, beautified with broad fire-shelters, and carpeted with kuśa grass.

sanskrit: vibhūṣitaṃ puṇyapavitratoyayā; sadā ca juṣṭaṃ nṛpa jahnukanyayā mahātmabhir dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhair; maharṣibhir bhūṣitam agnikalpaiḥ
english: Adorned, O king, by the daughter of Jahnu with her holy and purifying waters, ever-frequented by her, it was graced by great-souled seers, foremost among upholders of dharma, who blazed like fire.

sanskrit: vāyvāhārair ambupair japyanityaiḥ; saṃprakṣālair yatibhir dhyānanityaiḥ dhūmāśanair ūṣmapaiḥ kṣīrapaiś ca; vibhūṣitaṃ brāhmaṇendraiḥ samantāt
english: It was adorned all around by foremost brāhmaṇas—ascetics who lived on air, who drank only water, who were ever at their muttered prayers, who scoured their vessels clean, who were ever in meditation, who fed on smoke, who drank only warmth, and who lived upon milk alone.

sanskrit: gocāriṇo 'thāśmakuṭṭā dantolūkhalinas tathā marīcipāḥ phenapāś ca tathaiva mṛgacāriṇaḥ
english: There were those who grazed like cattle, those who ground their grain on stones, those whose mortar was their own teeth, those who lived on the sun's rays, those who drank only foam, and those who roamed like the wild deer.

sanskrit: suduḥkhān niyamāṃs tāṃs tān vahataḥ sutaponvitān paśyann utphullanayanaḥ praveṣṭum upacakrame
english: Beholding these men who upheld their grievous vows in the rigour of austerity, with wide-open eyes I set myself to enter in.

sanskrit: supūjitaṃ devagaṇair mahātmabhiḥ; śivādibhir bhārata puṇyakarmabhiḥ rarāja tac cāśramamaṇḍalaṃ sadā; divīva rājan ravimaṇḍalaṃ yathā
english: Well honoured by the hosts of gods, the great-souled ones, Śiva and the rest, doers of holy deeds, O Bhārata, that circle of hermitage ever shone, O king, like the orb of the sun in the heavens.

sanskrit: krīḍanti sarpair nakulā mṛgair vyāghrāś ca mitravat prabhāvād dīptatapasaḥ saṃnikarṣaguṇānvitāḥ
english: There the mongooses sported with the serpents, and the tigers with the deer, as friends—through the power and the virtue of nearness to those whose austerity blazed forth.

sanskrit: tatrāśramapade śreṣṭhe sarvabhūtamanorame sevite dvijaśārdūlair vedavedāṅgapāragaiḥ
english: In that supreme hermitage, delightful to all beings, frequented by tigers among the twice-born who had mastered the Vedas and their auxiliaries—

sanskrit: nānāniyamavikhyātair ṛṣibhiś ca mahātmabhiḥ praviśann eva cāpaśyaṃ jaṭācīradharaṃ prabhum
english: —and by great-souled sages renowned for their manifold vows, even as I entered I beheld the Lord, wearing matted locks and bark-cloth garments.

sanskrit: tejasā tapasā caiva dīpyamānaṃ yathānalam śiṣyamadhyagataṃ śāntaṃ yuvānaṃ brāhmaṇarṣabham śirasā vandamānaṃ mām upamanyur abhāṣata
english: Blazing like fire with splendour and with austerity, seated amid his pupils, serene, youthful, a bull among brāhmaṇas—Upamanyu spoke to me as I bowed my head before him.

sanskrit: svāgataṃ puṇḍarīkākṣa saphalāni tapāṃsi naḥ yat pūjyaḥ pūjayasi no draṣṭavyo draṣṭum icchasi
english: "Welcome, O lotus-eyed one. Our austerities have borne their fruit, since you who are worthy of worship pay us honour, and you who are worthy to be beheld desire to behold us."

sanskrit: tam ahaṃ prāñjalir bhūtvā mṛgapakṣiṣv athāgniṣu dharme ca śiṣyavarge ca samapṛccham anāmayam
english: Then, with palms joined together, I asked after the welfare of his beasts and birds, of his sacred fires, of his observance of dharma, and of the band of his pupils.

sanskrit: tato māṃ bhagavān āha sāmnā paramavalgunā lapsyase tanayaṃ kṛṣṇa ātmatulyam asaṃśayam
english: Then the blessed sage said to me with words most gentle and kind: "You shall surely obtain, O Kṛṣṇa, a son who is your own equal—of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: tapaḥ sumahad āsthāya toṣayeśānam īśvaram iha devaḥ sapatnīkaḥ samākrīḍaty adhokṣaja
english: "Undertaking a most mighty austerity, propitiate the Lord, the Ruler; for here, O Adhokṣaja, the god disports himself together with his consort."

sanskrit: ihaiva devatāśreṣṭhaṃ devāḥ sarṣigaṇāḥ purā tapasā brahmacaryeṇa satyena ca damena ca toṣayitvā śubhān kāmān prāpnuvaṃs te janārdana
english: "In this very place, O Janārdana, the gods together with the hosts of sages, in days of old, having gratified that best of deities by austerity, by chastity, by truth and by self-restraint, obtained their fair desires."

sanskrit: tejasāṃ tapasāṃ caiva nidhiḥ sa bhagavān iha śubhāśubhānvitān bhāvān visṛjan saṃkṣipann api āste devyā sahācintyo yaṃ prārthayasi śatruhan
english: "That blessed Lord, the treasure-house of all splendours and austerities, dwells here together with the Goddess—he, the inconceivable one, who sends forth and withdraws all states of being, both fair and foul—the very one whom you entreat, O slayer of foes."

sanskrit: hiraṇyakaśipur yo 'bhūd dānavo merukampanaḥ tena sarvāmaraiśvaryaṃ śarvāt prāptaṃ samārbudam
english: "Hiraṇyakaśipu, the dānava who once shook Mount Meru, obtained from Śarva the lordship over all the immortals for a full ten million years."

sanskrit: tasyaiva putrapravaro mandaro nāma viśrutaḥ mahādevavarāc chakraṃ varṣārbudam ayodhayat
english: "His foremost son, renowned as Mandara, by a boon of Mahādeva did battle with Śakra for ten million years."

sanskrit: viṣṇoś cakraṃ ca tad ghoraṃ vajram ākhaṇḍalasya ca śīrṇaṃ purābhavat tāta grahasyāṅgeṣu keśava
english: "Even the dread discus of Viṣṇu and the thunderbolt of Ākhaṇḍala, O dear Keśava, were of old shattered upon the limbs of that demon Graha."

sanskrit: ardyamānāś ca vibudhā graheṇa subalīyasā śivadattavarāñ jaghnur asurendrān surā bhṛśam
english: "And the gods, sorely oppressed by that mighty Graha, slew in their turn many a lord of the asuras who had been granted boons by Śiva."

sanskrit: tuṣṭo vidyutprabhasyāpi trilokeśvaratām adāt śataṃ varṣasahasrāṇāṃ sarvalokeśvaro 'bhavat mamaivānucaro nityaṃ bhavitāsīti cābravīt
english: "Well pleased with Vidyutprabha too, he gave him the sovereignty of the three worlds; for a hundred thousand years he became the lord of all worlds, and the god said: 'You shall ever be my attendant.'"

sanskrit: tathā putrasahasrāṇām ayutaṃ ca dadau prabhuḥ kuśadvīpaṃ ca sa dadau rājyena bhagavān ajaḥ
english: "Likewise the Lord granted him ten thousand sons, and the blessed Unborn one gave him the island of Kuśa to rule as a kingdom."

sanskrit: tathā śatamukho nāma dhātrā sṛṣṭo mahāsuraḥ yena varṣaśataṃ sāgram ātmamāṃsair huto 'nalaḥ taṃ prāha bhagavāṃs tuṣṭaḥ kiṃ karomīti śaṃkaraḥ
english: "So too there was a great asura named Śatamukha, fashioned by the Creator, who for a full hundred years offered up the fire with his own flesh; and the blessed Śaṃkara, well pleased, said to him: 'What shall I do for you?'"

sanskrit: taṃ vai śatamukhaḥ prāha yogo bhavatu me 'dbhutaḥ balaṃ ca daivataśreṣṭha śāśvataṃ saṃprayaccha me
english: "And Śatamukha answered him: 'Let mine be a wondrous power of yoga, and grant me, O best of the gods, strength that endures forever.'"

sanskrit: svāyaṃbhuvaḥ kratuś cāpi putrārtham abhavat purā āviśya yogenātmānaṃ trīṇi varṣaśatāny api
english: "And Kratu, son of the Self-existent, of old, longing for offspring, entered into himself through yoga for three hundred years."

sanskrit: tasya devo 'dadat putrān sahasraṃ kratusaṃmitān yogeśvaraṃ devagītaṃ vettha kṛṣṇa na saṃśayaḥ
english: "To him the god granted a thousand sons, each the equal of Kratu himself. You know, O Kṛṣṇa, the Lord of yoga who is sung of by the gods—of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: vālakhilyā maghavatā avajñātāḥ purā kila taiḥ kruddhair bhagavān rudras tapasā toṣito hy abhūt
english: "The Vālakhilyas, it is said, were once slighted by Maghavat; and they in their wrath gratified the blessed Rudra by their austerities."

sanskrit: tāṃś cāpi daivataśreṣṭhaḥ prāha prīto jagatpatiḥ suparṇaṃ somahartāraṃ tapasotpādayiṣyatha
english: "And to them the best of gods, the Lord of the world, well pleased, declared: 'By your austerity you shall bring forth Suparṇa, the carrier-off of the soma.'"

sanskrit: mahādevasya roṣāc ca āpo naṣṭāḥ purābhavan tāś ca saptakapālena devair anyāḥ pravartitāḥ
english: "Through the wrath of Mahādeva the waters of old were destroyed, and the gods brought other waters into being by means of the seven-skulled rite."

sanskrit: atrer bhāryāpi bhartāraṃ saṃtyajya brahmavādinī nāhaṃ tasya muner bhūyo vaśagā syāṃ kathaṃ cana ity uktvā sā mahādevam agacchac charaṇaṃ kila
english: "The wife of Atri too, a speaker of sacred truth, forsook her husband, saying: 'Never again shall I be subject to the will of that sage'; and so saying she went, it is said, for refuge to Mahādeva."

sanskrit: nirāhārā bhayād atres trīṇi varṣaśatāny api aśeta musaleṣv eva prasādārthaṃ bhavasya sā
english: "Taking no food, in fear of Atri, she lay even upon pestles for three hundred years, to win the grace of Bhava."

sanskrit: tām abravīd dhasan devo bhavitā vai sutas tava vaṃśe tavaiva nāmnā tu khyātiṃ yāsyati cepsitām
english: "To her the god said, smiling: 'A son shall surely be born to you, and in your own line he shall attain the renown you desire, bearing your name.'"

sanskrit: śākalyaḥ saṃśitātmā vai nava varṣaśatāny api ārādhayām āsa bhavaṃ manoyajñena keśava
english: "Śākalya, a man of disciplined soul, propitiated Bhava for nine hundred years with the sacrifice of the mind, O Keśava."

sanskrit: taṃ cāha bhagavāṃs tuṣṭo granthakāro bhaviṣyasi vatsākṣayā ca te kīrtis trailokye vai bhaviṣyati akṣayaṃ ca kulaṃ te 'stu maharṣibhir alaṃkṛtam
english: "And the blessed Lord, well pleased, said to him: 'You shall become an author of treatises, my child; your fame shall be imperishable throughout the three worlds, and let your lineage be undying, adorned with great sages.'"

sanskrit: sāvarṇiś cāpi vikhyāta ṛṣir āsīt kṛte yuge iha tena tapas taptaṃ ṣaṣṭiṃ varṣaśatāny atha
english: "There was too a renowned sage named Sāvarṇi in the Kṛta age; here he practised austerity for six thousand years."

sanskrit: tam āha bhagavān rudraḥ sākṣāt tuṣṭo 'smi te 'nagha granthakṛl lokavikhyāto bhavitāsy ajarāmaraḥ
english: "To him the blessed Rudra appeared in person and said: 'I am pleased with you, O sinless one. You shall become a maker of treatises, renowned throughout the world, free of age and death.'"

sanskrit: mayāpi ca yathā dṛṣṭo devadevaḥ purā vibhuḥ sākṣāt paśupatis tāta tac cāpi śṛṇu mādhava
english: "And how I too of old beheld in person the God of gods, the all-pervading Lord, Paśupati himself, of that also hear, dear Mādhava."

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ ca mahādevaḥ prayatena mayā purā ārādhito mahātejās tac cāpi śṛṇu vistaram
english: "And for what purpose I once, with strenuous effort, propitiated the mighty Mahādeva of great splendour—that too hear in full."

sanskrit: yad avāptaṃ ca me pūrvaṃ devadevān maheśvarāt tat sarvam akhilenādya kathayiṣyāmi te 'nagha
english: "And whatever I formerly gained from the God of gods, from Maheśvara, all of that, entire and without omission, I shall now relate to you, O sinless one."

sanskrit: purā kṛtayuge tāta ṛṣir āsīn mahāyaśāḥ vyāghrapāda iti khyāto vedavedāṅgapāragaḥ tasyāham abhavaṃ putro dhaumyaś cāpi mamānujaḥ
english: "Long ago, in the Kṛta age, my dear one, there lived a sage of great renown, known as Vyāghrapad, master of the Vedas and their auxiliaries. I was his son, and Dhaumya was my younger brother."

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya dhaumyena saha mādhava āgaccham āśramaṃ krīḍan munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām
english: "Now once upon a time, O Mādhava, I came at play, together with Dhaumya, to the hermitage of sages whose souls were purified."

sanskrit: tatrāpi ca mayā dṛṣṭā duhyamānā payasvinī lakṣitaṃ ca mayā kṣīraṃ svāduto hy amṛtopamam
english: "And there I saw a milk-cow being milked, and I marked that its milk was sweet to the taste, like the very nectar of immortality."

sanskrit: tataḥ piṣṭaṃ samāloḍya toyena saha mādhava āvayoḥ kṣīram ity eva pānārtham upanīyate
english: "Now flour, O Mādhava, stirred together with water, used to be brought to the two of us to drink, under the name of 'milk.'"

sanskrit: atha gavyaṃ payas tāta kadā cit prāśitaṃ mayā tataḥ piṣṭarasaṃ tāta na me prītim udāvahat
english: "Then once, my dear one, I tasted the milk of a cow, and thereafter the flour-water, O dear one, no longer gave me any pleasure."

sanskrit: tato 'ham abruvaṃ bālyāj jananīm ātmanas tadā kṣīrodanasamāyuktaṃ bhojanaṃ ca prayaccha me
english: "Then in my childish way I said to my own mother: 'Give me food made with milk-porridge to eat.'"

sanskrit: tato mām abravīn mātā duḥkhaśokasamanvitā putrasnehāt pariṣvajya mūrdhni cāghrāya mādhava
english: "Then my mother, filled with grief and sorrow, embracing me out of a mother's love and kissing me upon the head, O Mādhava, said to me:"

sanskrit: kutaḥ kṣīrodanaṃ vatsa munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām vane nivasatāṃ nityaṃ kandamūlaphalāśinām
english: "'Whence is milk-porridge to come, my child, for sages of purified souls who dwell ever in the forest and feed upon roots, bulbs and fruits?'"

sanskrit: aprasādya virūpākṣaṃ varadaṃ sthāṇum avyayam kutaḥ kṣīrodanaṃ vatsa sukhāni vasanāni ca
english: "'Without first winning the grace of the three-eyed Virūpākṣa, the giver of boons, the unmoving and undecaying Sthāṇu—whence, my child, is milk-porridge to come, or comforts, or fine raiment?'"
